kernel: A horror story. On a wild night an old soldier back from India visits your family's cottage at the end of a lonely road, and shows you a mummified paw that he says grants three wishes. He begs you to burn it. I want the wishes to come true in the worst possible way, and the dread to build slowly from something small. No gore.

mediation.question: If fate punishes those who interfere with it, what do you wish for when the first wish has cost everything?

T1.title: Three Wishes
T1.motivation: You start out wanting a little money to clear the house; you end wanting only to undo what you wished.

ending.title: The Empty Road
ending.summary: The knocking stops. Your wife opens the door on an empty road and a streetlamp flickering on nothing; your son stays dead, and you are the one who made sure of it.
ending.changed: the money is paid, the son is buried, and the last wish was spent to keep him so

N01.title: Check
N01.summary: Laburnam Villa, a raw wet night. You play chess with your son Herbert and lose, because you put your king into needless danger; you grumble about living at the end of a road nobody else lives on. Your wife knits by the fire and tells you that you'll win next time.
N01.image: a chessboard by the fire, the king left open

N02.title: The Sergeant-Major's Paw
N02.summary: Sergeant-Major Morris, back from twenty-one years in India, drinks your whisky and tells stories, then shows you a little mummified paw. An old fakir put a spell on it to show that fate rules lives: three men can have three wishes. The first man's third wish was for death.
N02.image: a dried, shrivelled paw on the table

N03.title: Out of the Fire
N03.summary: Morris throws the paw on the fire. You snatch it out. He begs you to let it burn, then tells you how to wish, and warns you to wish for something sensible. Herbert laughs: wish to be an emperor, father, then you won't be henpecked.
N03.image: a paw snatched from the coals, smelling of smoke

N04.title: Two Hundred Pounds
N04.summary: To clear the house you wish for two hundred pounds. The paw twists in your hand like a snake. Nothing else happens. Herbert jokes about the money in a bag on the bed and something horrible on the wardrobe; in the dying fire he sees a monkey's face.
N04.image: the paw twisting like a snake in your hand

N05.title: Maw and Meggins
N05.summary: A stranger in good clothes walks past your gate three times before opening it. He is from Maw and Meggins, where Herbert works. Herbert was caught in the machinery. The firm admits no liability, but in consideration of your son's services offers a sum: two hundred pounds.
N05.image: a well-dressed man pacing past the gate three times

N06.title: The Second Wish
N06.summary: A week after the funeral your wife wakes you: the paw! Two wishes left. Wish him alive. You tell her he was ten days dead, that you knew him only by his clothes. She drags you down to the cold parlour, and you wish your son alive again.
N06.image: the paw on the mantelpiece in the cold parlour

N07.title: The Knocking
N07.summary: A knock at the door, quiet and stealthy. Your wife runs to it crying that it is Herbert; you hold her; she breaks free and fights the bolt she cannot reach. Knock after knock shakes the house while you crawl on the floor, hunting for the paw in the dark.
N07.image: a bolt at the top of the door, too high for her to reach

N08.title: The Empty Road
N08.summary: You find the paw and breathe your third wish as the bolt slides back. The knocking stops. Your wife's long wail; you run to her and look out at a quiet, empty road under a flickering lamp.
N08.image: a streetlamp flickering on an empty road

C01.label: the old soldier
C01.name: Sergeant-Major Morris
C01.wants: to be rid of the paw and to warn you
C01.edge: has used his three wishes and will not say what they were
C01.voice: "If you must wish, wish for something sensible."

C02.label: your son
C02.name: Herbert White
C02.voice: "Well, I don't see the money, and I bet I never shall."

C03.label: your wife
C03.name: Mrs White
C03.wants: her son back at any price
C03.edge: grief that will not be argued with
C03.voice: "Go down and get it quickly, and wish our boy alive again."
C03.breaking_point: turns on you when you refuse the second wish

C04.label: the man from the firm
C04.name: the man from Maw and Meggins
C04.wants: to deliver his message and leave
C04.edge: kind, careful, and the messenger of the wish
